text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Six solar farms of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED), daylight hours, March 2024 to April 2026. IFS: ECMWF's forecast via Open-Meteo. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Dashed rule: no difference. Each row is the error of F6 without the variables that one group adds, minus the error of F6. Error: mean absolute error. Positive means removing the group raised the error. A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given, beside sun position and calendar. F0: IFS radiation and air temperature. Each set adds to the one before. F1: total cloud cover. F2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. F3: direct radiation. F4: dew point, column water vapour, boundary-layer height. F5: convective energy (CAPE), inhibition, visibility. F6 (all 20 IFS variables): surface and weather variables. IFS: ECMWF's 9 km forecast, 00 UTC run, read at a lead day. Lead day L: the forecast was issued L days before the day it describes, so lead day 1 is the morning before. Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.'
text.tspan: Six solar farms of National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED), daylight hours, March 2024 to April 2026. IFS:
Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Dashed rule: no difference. Each row is the error
of F6 without the variables that one group adds, minus the error of F6. Error: mean absolute error. Positive means
removing the group raised the error.
A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given, beside sun position and calendar.
F0: IFS radiation and air temperature. Each set adds to the one before. F1: total cloud cover. F2: low, mid, and
high cloud cover. F3: direct radiation. F4: dew point, column water vapour, boundary-layer height. F5: convective
energy (CAPE), inhibition, visibility. F6 (all 20 IFS variables): surface and weather variables.
IFS: ECMWF's 9 km forecast, 00 UTC run, read at a lead day.
Lead day L: the forecast was issued L days before the day it describes, so lead day 1 is the morning before.
Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.
